question:
A company plans to produce three products $A_{1}, A_{2}, A_{3}$. It can produce for 22 days in a month. The table below gives the maximum demand (in units of 100 kg), prices ($\$/100 \mathrm{~Kg}$), production costs (per 100 kg of product), and production quotas (the maximum number of units of 100 kg of product that can be produced in a day if all production lines are dedicated to that product).

| Product | $A_{1}$ | $A_{2}$ | $A_{3}$ |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Maximum Demand | 5300 | 4500 | 5400 |
| Selling Price | $\$ 124$ | $\$ 109$ | $\$ 115$ |
| Production Cost | $\$ 73.30$ | $\$ 52.90$ | $\$ 65.40$ |
| Production Quota | 500 | 450 | 550 |

The fixed activation cost for each production line is as follows:

| Product | $A_{1}$ | $A_{2}$ | $A_{3}$ |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Activation Cost | $\$ 170000$ | $\$ 150000$ | $\$ 100000$ |

The minimum production batch sizes are as follows:
$$
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
\text { Product } & A_{1} & A_{2} & A_{3} \\
\hline \text { Minimum Batch Size } & 20 & 20 & 16
\end{array}
$$
Please formulate an operations research model to determine the production plan that maximizes total revenue while accommodating the fixed activation costs and minimum production batch size restrictions.

DATA = {
    # "It can produce for 22 days in a month."
    "days": 22,
    # Products set
    "products": ["A1", "A2", "A3"],
    # "Maximum Demand" row (units of 100 kg)
    "max_demand": {"A1": 5300, "A2": 4500, "A3": 5400},
    # "Selling Price" row ($/100 kg)
    "price": {"A1": 124, "A2": 109, "A3": 115},
    # "Production Cost" row ($/100 kg)
    "cost": {"A1": 73.30, "A2": 52.90, "A3": 65.40},
    # "Production Quota": units of 100 kg producible per day if dedicated
    "quota": {"A1": 500, "A2": 450, "A3": 550},
    # "Activation Cost" for each production line ($)
    "activation": {"A1": 170000, "A2": 150000, "A3": 100000},
    # "Minimum Batch Size" (units of 100 kg)
    "min_batch": {"A1": 20, "A2": 20, "A3": 16},
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Set ---
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])

    # --- Variables ---
    # Production quantity of each product (units of 100 kg).
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.P,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=lambda m, p: (0, d["max_demand"][p]),
    )
    # Activation binary for each production line.
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # --- Objective: maximize profit = net margin * qty - activation costs ---
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(
            (d["price"][p] - d["cost"][p]) * m.x[p] for p in m.P
        ) - sum(d["activation"][p] * m.y[p] for p in m.P)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # --- Constraints ---

    # Capacity: production requires the line to be activated and cannot
    # exceed the total producible amount over the available days.
    def cap_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] <= d["quota"][p] * d["days"] * m.y[p]

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=cap_rule)

    # Maximum demand upper bound (redundant with var bound but explicit).
    def demand_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] <= d["max_demand"][p]

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=demand_rule)

    # Minimum batch size: if activated, must produce at least the batch size.
    def minbatch_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] >= d["min_batch"][p] * m.y[p]

    model.min_batch = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=minbatch_rule)

    return model

        model.P,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=lambda m, p: (0, d["max_demand"][p]),
    )

    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, domain=pyo.Binary)

#
# Decision variables
#   x[i]  : production quantity of product i (units of 100 kg), NonNegativeReals,
#           bounded above by maximum demand.
#   y[i]  : binary activation indicator for product i's production line.
#
# Objective (maximize)
#   Net profit = sum_i (price_i - cost_i) * x[i]  -  sum_i activation_i * y[i]
#
# Constraints
#   (1) Max demand:        x[i] <= max_demand[i]                       for all i
#   (2) Time budget:       sum_i x[i] / quota[i] <= days_available
#                          (linear: sum_i (1/quota[i]) * x[i] <= days_available)
#   (3) Min batch linking: x[i] >= min_batch[i] * y[i]                 for all i
#   (4) Activation linking: x[i] <= max_demand[i] * y[i]               for all i
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "products": ["A1", "A2", "A3"],
    "max_demand": {"A1": 5300, "A2": 4500, "A3": 5400},
    "price": {"A1": 124.0, "A2": 109.0, "A3": 115.0},
    "cost": {"A1": 73.30, "A2": 52.90, "A3": 65.40},
    "quota": {"A1": 500, "A2": 450, "A3": 550},
    "activation": {"A1": 170000.0, "A2": 150000.0, "A3": 100000.0},
    "min_batch": {"A1": 20, "A2": 20, "A3": 16},
    "days_available": 22,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = d["products"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products)

    # Decision variables
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.P,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=lambda m, i: (0, d["max_demand"][i]),
    )
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: maximize net profit
    def obj_rule(m):
        revenue = sum((d["price"][i] - d["cost"][i]) * m.x[i] for i in m.P)
        fixed = sum(d["activation"][i] * m.y[i] for i in m.P)
        return revenue - fixed

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # (1) Max demand
    def max_demand_rule(m, i):
        return m.x[i] <= d["max_demand"][i]

    model.max_demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=max_demand_rule)

    # (2) Time budget: sum_i x[i]/quota[i] <= days_available
    def time_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[i] / d["quota"][i] for i in m.P) <= d["days_available"]

    model.time_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=time_rule)

    # (3) Minimum batch linking: x[i] >= min_batch[i] * y[i]
    def min_batch_rule(m, i):
        return m.x[i] >= d["min_batch"][i] * m.y[i]

    model.min_batch_con = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=min_batch_rule)

    # (4) Activation linking: x[i] <= max_demand[i] * y[i]
    def activation_rule(m, i):
        return m.x[i] <= d["max_demand"][i] * m.y[i]

    model.activation_con = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=activation_rule)

    return model
